diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and step 1.2: x=s omega with fixed omega in S^(d-1) gives -R(t)<s<R(t). Left vertices have radii 1 and 1.9 over height 3, so c=0.3 and R0=1; both radii positive. The four edges are two cap sections and two lateral sections. Caption makes c>0 representative and retains c<=0 cases. This section is valid for every d>=1.

Step 1.2 gives bottom -e_t and top +e_t, drawn down/up. Step 2.1 gives right-side gradient (omega,-c). Left panel right tangent (0.9,3) has dot product zero with arrow displacement (0.9,-0.27), and the arrow points toward increasing s, outside g<0. The arrow therefore has precisely the direction (omega,-0.3); normalization is stated in the caption.

Step 4.1 uses c>0, R(t)=c(t-a0). Right apex (0,0), upper radius 1.8 at height 3 and truncation radius 0.48 at height 0.8 all satisfy R=0.6(t-a0). Solid lower edge is the artificial cap with downward arrow. Two dashed segments run from its endpoints to the apex and indicate only omitted lateral boundary; the volume leader originates inside that small triangle. No apex chart, normal or smoothness is assigned.

Step 4.1 explicitly bounds cap flux by M v_d (c delta)^d, side flux by M sqrt(1+c^2) v_d c^(d-1) delta^d and volume integral by L v_d c^d delta^(d+1)/(d+1). The new caption only summarizes these existing orders. Existing rigorous verification is byte-preserved and independent of the illustration.
